vote.question: FUTARCHY CONDITIONAL RESOLUTION [US-AL U.S. Senate]: Felix Barry Moore (R) has accumulated $11,440,101 in career FEC-reported receipts (anchored this cycle by Senate Opportunity Fund ($2,820,000) and $4,363,500 from top-5 patrons)—out-raising general opponent Everett W Wess ($128,570) by 88.98x—exhibiting the "Extractive Energy & Petrochemical Capture" profile. Will independent constituent & oracle review confirm that this private-interest capital concentration compromises public representation in US-AL, thereby executing the AL Corrective Restitution Pool toward clean water remediation, community grid resilience, and environmental health clinics?
vote.futarchy_thesis: Private campaign financing treats US-AL representation as an investable asset class. When Felix Barry Moore's campaign apparatus absorbs $11,440,101 (anchored this cycle by Senate Opportunity Fund ($2,820,000) and $4,363,500 from top-5 patrons), policy incentives skew toward regulatory leniency toward industrial emissions, grid monopolies, and watershed externalities. This futarchy market converts spectator outrage into direct fiscal counter-leverage.
options: Yes — Confirm Capture & Execute State Restitution Bounty
No — Veto Capture Claim & Roll Escrow Pool to Bipartisan Commons
Abstain — Log On-Chain Constituent Dissent Only

outcomes.YES_EXECUTE_RESTITUTION: Confirms special-interest capture; releases 100% of escrowed pool to audited state 501(c)(3) restitution beneficiaries — direct corrective remediation of the captured constituent impact.

outcomes.ABSTAIN_AUDIT_ONLY: Logs cryptographic constituent dissent on-chain without shifting conditional odds; preserves the pool for future cycle reconsideration.

If the No option wins, funds redirect to a bipartisan district-wide common good that strengthens the entire community — denying special interests the ability to commandeer the bounty and promoting positive-sum governance over zero-sum subjugation.
